Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Louise Schiavone. Five men have been arrested on suspicion of planning to attack a British air base used by the U.S. military in the Iran war.
NPR's Kristin Wright reports authorities have not named the suspects.
British police arrested the five men after reports of three suspicious vehicles heading toward the base.
The men are suspected of plotting to carry out a terrorist attack involving explosives at RAF Fairford in western England about 100 miles from London.
The U.S. Air Force uses the Royal Air Force Base for defensive operations against Iran and deploys large bombers to launch limited strikes in the war.
President Trump told reporters the suspects were looking to do big damage and had been watched for a long time.
American troops have used the base for decades under an agreement dating back to the 1950s.
Kristin Wright, NPR News.
A little more than a month away from midterm elections, trend watchers are following favorability ratings for signs of how the outcomes will affect the political balance of power.
NPR's Marah Liasen tells us it doesn't appear either party is poised to glide into victory in the U.S. Senate.
There is some good news for Republicans in some Senate races, and Senate races often depend more on candidate quality than the national political environment.
So in Michigan and Maine and New Hampshire, you see Republicans with pretty strong candidates holding their own.
Susan Collins, the incumbent in Maine, Mike Rogers in Michigan, John Sununu in New Hampshire.
Those races are in states that Democrats should be the favorites, but they're struggling in all three of them.
All three of those races are considered toss-ups.
And remember, the Democrats need to net four pickups to take back control of the Senate.
And PR's Marah Liasen, in Hawaii, Hurricane NOLO continues to move away from the island chain.
The storm has now become a major hurricane with wind speeds topping 111 miles an hour.
But as Hawaii Public Radio's Bill Dorman reports, the increasing wind speeds are not causing major damage.
NOLO's growing intensity has pushed it to a Category 3 hurricane, but it's moved far enough south of Hawaii that it's not bearing down on the main island chain.
The storm's impacts are lingering.
Strong and gusty winds are whipping across several islands, especially Maui and Hawaii Island.
That's knocked out power to several thousand people, and floodwaters have swept through some areas.
Even so, the storm did not cause as much damage as feared.
Hurricane NOLO is expected to reach its peak intensity Monday, even further from Hawaii's shores.
For NPR News, I'm Bill Dorman in Honolulu.
Drenching rain continued to saturate shorelines in the northeastern U.S. today.
Another round of flooding hit low-lying areas of New York and New Jersey and led to power outages in multiple northeastern states.
A falling tree in Brooklyn killed a New York Housing Authority worker.
Travel by land and air has been disrupted.
This is NPR News in Washington.
Chinese pandas Pingping and Fuchuang are now at Zoo Atlanta, having traveled from Chengdu in southwestern China aboard a specialized FedEx Panda Express.
It's part of a new agreement between the U.S. and Chinese governments.
The loan of pandas is part of China's global diplomacy program.
The name of the male, Pingping, means "peaceful."
The female's name, Fuchuang, means "double happiness."
These pandas will stay for 10 years.
Researchers in Canada have discovered two new species that are related to spiders, and PR Chantaliz Duster has more.
Two new species of sea spiders have been discovered by researchers at the University of British Columbia in Canada.
They were found in the Salish Sea between Washington State and the Canadian province of British Columbia.
One of the new sea spider species has red eyes and hairy legs.
Cormac Tolar Scott, who led the research that discovered the new species, says they won't appear crawling across your living room floor.
They have a hard time on land. They really need to be in the water.
They're quite slow-moving. They just kind of crawl on the sea floor.
Scientists have discovered more than 1,300 species of sea spiders.
While the new species are related to spiders, they are also different.
They don't have venom or fangs and mainly rely on camouflage to defend themselves.
Chantaliz Duster, NPR News.
At the box office this weekend, Avengers Endgame returned to the top spot in a victory lap for Marvel,
and an appetizer for the upcoming Avengers Doomsday the re-release grossed $26 million.
I'm Louise Schiavone, NPR News, Washington.
